extracted.intended_audience: The people and electors of the State of New York; citizens and policymakers considering ratification of the U.S. Constitution
extracted.subtask_description: A persuasive political essay (The Federalist No. XLV–XLVI) arguing the necessity, scope, and safeguards of federal powers versus state powers under the proposed U.S. Constitution. It explains specific constitutional provisions and the practical consequences of their application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on State coinage and multiplicity of mints
rubrics_metrics.description: States must not have a right of coinage that would multiply expensive mints and diversify the forms and weights of circulating pieces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowing each State to regulate coin would produce many different currencies, impede intercourse among States, enable retrospective alterations of value injuring citizens of other States, and discredit the Union. Local mints under general authority could achieve necessary ends without multiple state coinages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on State emission of bills of credit (paper money)
rubrics_metrics.description: The extension of the prohibition to bills of credit must give pleasure to every citizen... The power to emit paper money is withdrawn from the States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper money has damaged confidence between citizens and in public councils, harmed industry and morals, and corrupted republican government. States emitting paper money would produce mischiefs similar to separate coinage; thus the Constitution bars States from issuing bills of credit or making anything but gold and silver legal tender.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on States making anything but gold and silver a tender in payment of debts
rubrics_metrics.description: The power to make anything but gold and silver a tender in payment of debts is withdrawn from the States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This operates on the same principle as the prohibition on issuing paper currency: allowing states to declare other things legal tender would create multiple conflicting currencies and retrospective devaluations, harming interstate and foreign commerce and the Union's credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on bills of attainder, ex post facto laws, and laws impairing contracts by States
rubrics_metrics.description: Bills of attainder, ex-post-facto laws, and laws impairing the obligation of contracts are contrary to the first principles of the social compact... and are prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These prohibitions are additional constitutional 'fences' for personal security and private rights, intended to prevent legislative jobs, speculations on public measures, and repeated legislative interferences that injure the industrious and less-informed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on State imposts/duties on imports and exports
rubrics_metrics.description: No State shall, without the consent of the Congress, lay any imposts or duties on imports or exports, except what may be absolutely necessary for executing its inspection laws, and the net produce ... shall be for the use of the treasury of the United States; and all such laws shall be subject to the revision and control of the Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restraint secures uniform regulation of trade by federal councils while allowing states reasonable discretion for convenient inspections. It prevents conflicting state tariffs and ensures revenues from such duties go to the federal treasury under congressional oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on State powers re tonnage, troops, treaties, and war
rubrics_metrics.description: No State shall, without the consent of Congress, lay any duty on tonnage, keep troops or ships of war in time of peace, enter into any agreement or compact with another State, or with a foreign power, or engage in war unless actually invaded, or in such imminent danger as will not admit of delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These limits prevent individual States from undermining national security, foreign relations, and uniformity in defense and commerce; they are justified by the necessity of centralized control over external and military matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessary and Proper Clause (power to make all laws necessary and proper)
rubrics_metrics.description: The power to make all laws which shall be necessary and proper for carrying into execution the foregoing powers, and all other powers vested by this Constitution in the government of the United States, or in any department or officer thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Without the substance of this power, the Constitution would be a dead letter. The essay rejects alternative forms (strict 'expressly delegated' rule, exhaustive positive enumeration, negative enumeration of exceptions, or silence). It explains that where an end is required, the means necessary to achieve it are authorized, and attempts to enumerate all particular means would be chimerical or self-defeating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctrine of implication: means authorized by ends
rubrics_metrics.description: No axiom is more clearly established in law, or in reason, than that wherever the end is required, the means are authorized; wherever a general power to do a thing is given, every particular power necessary for doing it is included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Necessary and Proper Clause embodies this doctrine; positive or negative exhaustive enumerations would either cripple government or inadvertently grant omitted powers. If Congress misconstrues this clause, remedies lie in the executive and judiciary, and ultimately with the people by elections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supremacy Clause: Constitution and federal laws are supreme law
rubrics_metrics.description: This Constitution and the laws of the United States which shall be made in pursuance thereof, and all treaties made, or which shall be made, under the authority of the United States, shall be the supreme law of the land, and the judges in every State shall be bound thereby, any thing in the constitution or laws of any State to the contrary notwithstanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Without federal supremacy the new government would be impotent; state constitutions could annul national authorities and produce confusion where treaties or laws affect some states but not others. Supremacy prevents inversion of head and members in the system of governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath/affirmation requirement for federal and state officers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Senators and Representatives, and the members of the several State legislatures, and all executive and judicial officers, both of the United States and the several States, shall be bound by oath or affirmation to support this Constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay defends binding state officers to support the federal Constitution because state officials will be instrumental in giving effect to federal provisions; federal officers need not be similarly bound to state constitutions because they will have no agency in carrying those state constitutions into effect. The requirement helps secure fidelity to the federal system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy against unconstitutional exercises of power
rubrics_metrics.description: If Congress shall misconstrue this part of the Constitution, and exercise powers not warranted by its true meaning, the remedy... will depend on the executive and judiciary departments, and in the last resort a remedy must be obtained from the people who can, by the election of more faithful representatives, annul the acts of the usurpers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ultimate redress rests with the people through elections; the balance of state and federal interests and the vigilance of state legislatures make unconstitutional federal usurpations less likely, because states will be ready to sound alarm and exert influence to effect change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partitioning of powers: federal powers few and defined; state powers numerous and indefinite
rubrics_metrics.description: The powers delegated by the proposed Constitution to the federal government are few and defined. Those which are to remain in the State governments are numerous and indefinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal powers are mainly external (war, peace, negotiation, foreign commerce, taxation connected to those objects) and most important in war; state powers concern lives, liberties, properties, internal order, improvement, and prosperity, and are more active in times of peace. This partitioning reduces the risk of federal usurpation and preserves state influence through local offices and greater numbers of officers.
